title: Raise conditional κ to 0.003026674765 with a smaller completion reserve
body:
This certifies **conditional κ = 605334953/200000000000 = 0.003026674765**, exceeding Ali Romman’s PR #5383 value 0.00302666 by **0.000000014765**. The complete recursive profile is unchanged. This is a small finite compiler-margin improvement, not a new native mechanism or practical speedup.

Use tested saving 0.003026674766, reserve 10⁻¹², tensor power 1024 and the retained completion parameters. Two rational interval engines certify α < 1 − 10⁻¹² and both charged tails below 0.97. The exact completed bound is `1048576000976562501 / 1048576001073741824 < 1`. The old 10⁻⁹ reserve fails at this tested saving; 10⁻¹³ fails the fixed rounding budget. The finite compiler uses gap 1/7,000,000,000,000 and threshold `N = 2^409549000000000000`; all 54 strict and four functional outer predicates pass. The word is algorithmically specified, not expanded at that enormous threshold.

We reconstructed the eight compatible helper relations while #5383 was being published, then narrowed the contribution to this compiler-margin refinement. **Credit #5383 for the public eight-relation mechanism and prior bound; no priority claim is made for that construction.** The retained local witness has the same complete 64,148-paid / 10,800-target invoice, debits all 128 lost H9 targets, and preserves the rank surplus 752. It checks all 624 retained backward input columns and all 17 owned entry fields, with eight simultaneous snapshots; forward calls retain their original inputs. Our preparation ordering is priced afresh: scalar allowance 158,776, routes 4,834,000, total raw bound 181,098,496 < 10⁹.

Validation: registered normal and optimized Python 3.12 standard-library replays; exact row reduction and sixteen unrestricted source identities; chronological native frames, ownership, endpoints and phase-receipt inheritance; complete p16 controller/invoice; two interval engines; compiler/outer predicates; wrong-preparation controls for every pivot, other native controls and reserve/outer rejection controls; committed-byte checks, official export integrity and optimized read-only Git-free replay. The interpreter and pricing are adapted from #5377, not independently authored engines. No hosted CI, Lean/kernel check or human acceptance is claimed; full-history ancestry checking is not claimed in the shallow checkout.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eight-owned-relations
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/eight-owned-relations
```

The result retains the selected source’s native/all-size, owned-erasure, precision/tape, analytic, prime and recovery contracts. Physical precision/storage execution, source phase lowering and ordinary BIT construction are authenticated/reused rather than freshly executed. The #4610/#5241 admission and #5384 single-relation audit do not automatically admit this eight-relation endpoint. Selected-result metadata is unchanged. Larger draft #5270 is not used; #5349 documents its physical-reference/controller mismatch.

Credit Ali Romman #5377/#5383; Cao Yifan #4610; Chris R #5241/#5384; Cinna Davis #4470; zxv #5283 and completion/compiler work; Jacob Alan Sussman’s mixed-target recursion; Dugongue’s transported-frame lineage; ToikY and all retained native, Clifford, BIT, precision and analytic contributors. Smaller-reserve tightening already appears in #4610/#5241; the new result is its exact application to this eight-relation bill. Full source pins and frozen predecessor hashes are included.

One scoped package, based on canonical main 1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4, refreshed before release. Overlap checks covered 100 recently updated PRs, all 214 open search results containing “kappa”, and targeted bodies through #5384; Discussion coverage is incomplete. Prepared by Dugongue with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, solo. Apache-2.0. Open review questions are in README.md and TASK.json.
